skill.name: go-mod-helper
skill.description: Guides Go module setup, dependency management, private module access, workspaces, vendoring, CI, and release workflows.
skill.summary: Go module and dependency guidance for setup, updates, private repositories, workspaces, and release preparation.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown false positives from code fences, Go import and require syntax, module examples, and normal Go commands. I confirmed risks where the skill instructs handling plaintext tokens, netrc files, SSH private keys, and global credential or module configuration. No prompt-injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Replace direct .netrc token writing and default SSH private-key access with consent-gated steps, credential managers, and placeholder-free explanations.
Avoid credential.helper store. Prefer OS credential managers or CI-scoped environment variables, and warn before changing global Git configuration.
Scope GOPRIVATE, GONOPROXY, and GONOSUMDB to exact organization paths. Ask before persisting go env -w values.
Label destructive or persistent commands and require user confirmation for module cache cleanup, global configuration, and credential commands.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Git Credential Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends git credential.helper store for private repository access. This can persist Git credentials in plaintext and affects future Git commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance directly sets a global Git credential helper and follows it with global URL rewriting. This is a clear persistent credential-handling risk, although it is presented for a legitimate troubleshooting scenario.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Persistent Module Trust Configuration
semantic_findings.description: The private-module guidance sets persistent GOPRIVATE, GONOPROXY, and GONOSUMDB patterns. Overbroad patterns can bypass proxy or checksum controls for more modules than intended.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands use go env -w and broad wildcard patterns, so the changes persist beyond one project. This is normal Go private-module guidance but should be scoped and consent-gated.

content.value_statement: Go module setup and dependency updates can be error-prone across private repositories, workspaces, and releases. This skill provides command guidance for Go modules, dependency cleanup, versioning, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides go mod init, go.mod structure, and go.sum maintenance.
Shows dependency add, update, remove, download, verify, and tidy workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with Go module setup, dependency commands, private modules, workspaces, vendoring, CI examples, and common troubleshooting workflows.

faq.question: Can it edit go.mod for me?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance and review steps. Any file changes should be checked against your project requirements.

faq.question: Does it support private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains GOPRIVATE, Git URL rewriting, SSH, token-based access, and CI configuration patterns.

faq.question: Is credential setup automatic?
faq.answer: No. Credential commands are sensitive and should require explicit user approval before execution.

faq.question: Can it fix checksum mismatches?
faq.answer: It gives troubleshooting steps for cache cleanup, dependency download, tidy, verification, and GOSUMDB review.

faq.question: Does it replace security scanning?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated dependency vulnerability scanners and organization policy checks for security decisions.
